group.passage: In 1968, a tiny school in the mountains of Taitung became the talk of Taiwan. Hongye Elementary, in a village of the Bunun people, had only 114 students and five staff members, and its baseball players were said to practice with sticks for bats and stones for balls. The team's rise began that spring. After winning a youth tournament in Tainan in March, Hongye announced that it could not afford the trip to the national tournament in Taipei. Newspapers reported the problem, donations poured in, and the players traveled north and won the national title. Their greatest moment came on August 25, when, in front of about 20,000 fans, they defeated a visiting Japanese all-star team 7-0. No youth team from Taiwan had ever beaten a Japanese one before. Fans were so excited that they threw money onto the field, and the government promised the school funds for new equipment. The victory set off a baseball fever across the island. A year later, a Taiwanese team won the Little League World Series for the first time, and Taiwanese teams went on to collect seven more of these titles during the 1970s. For many people, Hongye was where it all started. Over time, however, the story grew larger than the facts. Many accounts claimed that Hongye had beaten Wakayama, the reigning world champions from Japan. Researchers later pointed out that this was hardly possible, since Wakayama was still playing in the United States until the day before the game. There was a darker side as well. In 1969, the team's coach and manager were found guilty of faking documents: some players were older than the rules allowed, and others did not even attend the school. Hongye itself never reached the Little League World Series. Even so, the village has not forgotten its summer of glory, and a memorial hall there displays old photos, equipment, and newspaper reports from that time. In 2026, the school won its first national Little League title, ending a 20-year wait for Taitung County.

translation_zh.text:
1968 年，台東山區一所小小的學校成為全台灣的話題。位於布農族部落的紅葉國小只有 114 名學生和五名教職員，據說它的棒球隊員是用木棍當球棒、用石頭當球來練習的。

這支球隊的崛起始於那年春天。紅葉在 3 月贏得台南的一場少年棒球賽之後，宣布付不起前往台北參加全國賽的旅費。報紙報導了這個難題，捐款隨即湧入，球員們北上並奪得全國冠軍。他們最輝煌的時刻是在 8 月 25 日：在大約兩萬名觀眾面前，他們以 7 比 0 擊敗來訪的日本明星隊。在此之前，台灣從來沒有一支少年球隊打贏過日本隊。球迷興奮得把錢丟進球場，政府也答應撥款給學校購買新的器材。

這場勝利在全島掀起了棒球熱潮。一年後，台灣球隊首度贏得世界少棒錦標賽冠軍，並在 1970 年代又拿下七座這項賽事的冠軍。對許多人來說，紅葉就是這一切的起點。

然而隨著時間過去，這個故事被傳得比事實更誇大。許多說法聲稱紅葉擊敗的是日本的衛冕世界冠軍和歌山隊。研究者後來指出這幾乎不可能，因為和歌山隊直到比賽前一天都還在美國比賽。這段歷史也有比較黑暗的一面。1969 年，球隊的教練和管理人員被判偽造文書：有些球員的年齡超過規定，有些甚至不是該校的學生。紅葉本身從未打進世界少棒錦標賽。

即便如此，部落並沒有忘記那個光榮的夏天，當地的紀念館展示著當年的老照片、器材和報紙報導。2026 年，紅葉國小贏得了學校第一座全國少棒聯盟（Little League）冠軍，終結了台東縣 20 年來的等待。
